bioAdditions:
Two census sheets attached to Andrew's FamilySearch profile close the gap between the 14-year-old of 1850 and the married man of 1880. On 7 August 1860 Andrew Pringle, 24, laborer, was living in Plymouth with Catharine, 23, and daughter Ellen, 2, in the dwelling immediately after that of James Pringle, 61, farmer, and Elizabeth, 57, with Edwin, 18 - the same James, Elizabeth and Edwin of the 1850 household (S1). This places Andrew, as an adult with Catherine Scott, next door to his parents, which is the documentary step an SAR/DAR application needs between the 1850 household and the 1880 family. On 29 July 1870 (indexed as 'Prindle') Andrew, 36, laborer, owned $500 in real estate; the household was Catharine 34, Ellen Jane 12, John 8, Samuel 7, Adison 5, Orange 3, an infant girl 'Julian' aged 4/12 (probably Julia Ann, named for Catherine's mother Julia Ann Scott) and James, 71 - evidently Andrew's widowed or separated father (S2).

The infant Julia(n) explains Catherine's later counts: she reported 7 children born and 5 living in 1900, when she was listed as divorced (S3), and 11 born/5 living as a widow in 1910 (S4). Ellen Jane, John, Samuel, Addison, Orange, Julia and Stella make seven; the two 'Ellen' and two 'Stella' profiles on FamilySearch are probably duplicates rather than extra children. Catherine's 1910 entry as 'widowed' supports Andrew's death before April 1910, consistent with the tree's 1900; in June 1900 she called herself divorced, which does not tell us whether he was then alive.

conflicts.assessment: 1850 (14), 1860 (24) and 1880 (44) all give c.1836; the 1870 age 36 is the outlier. Keep c.1836.

relationships.evidence: 1860: Andrew's household enumerated immediately after James Pringle's; 1870: James, 71, living in Andrew's household; 1850: Andrew 14 in James's household.

confidenceRecommendation.justification: 1850, 1860, 1870 and 1880 censuses now form a continuous chain: son in James's household (1850), married to Catharine next door to James (1860), James living with him (1870), and the 1880 household including Addison. Only a death record is missing.

openQuestionsResolved.question: 1860 census (Plymouth or Kingston) showing Andrew with Catherine and first children - ties the 1850 boy to the married man directly (top SAR step).
openQuestionsResolved.answer: Found: 1860 Plymouth, 7 Aug 1860, dwelling 879 Andrew 24, Catharine 23, Ellen 2, next door to James 61 & Elizabeth 57 & Edwin 18 (dwelling 878). The 1870 census also has James, 71, in Andrew's household.

openQuestionsNew: Who was the infant 'Julian' (4/12, female) in 1870 - presumably a daughter Julia Ann who died young (the 7th child)?
Who was Mary Williams, 7, in James Pringle's 1860 household (a grandchild?)

Death: Catherine was 'D' (divorced) in June 1900 and 'Wd' in April 1910, so Andrew died c.1900-1910; look for him in the 1900 census (possibly a boarder elsewhere in Luzerne) and in Wilkes-Barre papers.
